scope: M1 application binary attachments, exercised through existing response.body. Functional evidence only; no new performance or release claim.

implementation.framing: JSON start and terminal envelopes delimit request-scoped binary frames with exact encoded offsets and lengths. Raw bytes and canonical base64 groups are distinct encodings; the client exposes a Buffer only after complete terminal delivery.
implementation.resources: Negotiated defaults are 32 MiB decoded per payload and two active payloads. Producers use a one-frame channel and at most 64 KiB chunk payloads, obeying the control-frame cap. The writer interleaves replies/events and retains the payload reservation through terminal acknowledgement.
implementation.cancellation: Caller expiry releases partial assembled bytes while still validating late frames. Driver cancellation discards unsent chunks, sends one terminal error, and releases its slot. A failed or incomplete stream fails explicitly.
implementation.browserRepresentation: Existing Chromium base64 stays encoded until the Node receiver decodes bounded chunks. This removes a redundant Rust decode/re-encode but is not a measured speed claim.
implementation.diagnostics: Python lifecycle failures print tracebacks immediately, so a later watchdog cannot erase their diagnosis.

browser.executablePath: /Users/P/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium-1223/chrome-mac-arm64/Google Chrome for Testing.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome for Testing

acceptedChecks.payloadCoverage: Real Chromium tests cross a negotiated 32768-byte control cap with a 1 MiB binary body and UTF-8/NUL text. The synthetic client peer delivers a 9 MiB payload beyond the default 8 MiB control cap. That synthetic test is not coverage of a large CDP reply.

retainedFailures.assessment: The first empty-body fixture assumed the response event had arrived with the page-evaluation result and raised StopIteration. The corrected fixture waits explicitly for the independently delivered event. This exploratory run is not accepted final conformance.

The broad lifecycle batch exceeded its unchanged 240-second watchdog. Its first case also exhausted a 10-second aggregate subprocess budget around nine client launches. A separate instrumented rerun completed all nine scenarios and clean exits in 13.847 seconds. This diagnoses an inadequate aggregate fixture allowance; it does not turn the failed broad run into a pass. No owned process or profile residue remained.

remaining: Repair aggregate lifecycle fixture budgeting and complete the full Linux matrix; native Linux remains a separate gate.

The browser CDP reader still caps individual incoming messages at 8 MiB. Larger browser payload admission and failure behavior must be addressed before broad screenshot support; the application 32 MiB limit alone does not provide that coverage.
